grnland

Individual-based simulations of populations whose phenotypes are the steady states of gene regulatory networks (GRNs), evolving on arbitrary adaptive landscapes. This package generalises the simulation code behind Developmental Bias Shapes Evolution on Complex Adaptive Landscapes (Netz, Melo & Milocco) to networks with any number of genes and any regulatory structure.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("diogro/grnland", build_vignettes = TRUE)

The repository is private for now, so install_github() needs a GitHub token with access to it (usethis::create_github_token(), then set GITHUB_PAT). A C++ compiler is required (Rcpp/RcppArmadillo); ambient is needed for Perlin landscapes.

Quick start 

library(grnland)

m <- paper_motif(5)                                   # mutual activation
land <- landscape_gaussian(c(5, 3), omega = 4)        # one Gaussian peak
m_matrix(m, phenotype = c(2, 6))                      # mutational variance at the start
sim <- simulate_population(m, land, start = c(2, 6), N = 500, generations = 3000,
                           stop = stop_at_peaks(matrix(c(5, 3), 1)), seed = 1)
sim
plot(sim$trajectory$mean_x1, sim$trajectory$mean_x2, type = "l")

Models

Hill-type networks: grn()

For genes \(i = 1..n\),

\[\dot x_i = \alpha_i \prod_j H_{ij}(x_j) - \gamma_i x_i,\]

where \(H_{ij}(x) = x^h/(\theta^h + x^h)\) if gene \(j\) activates gene \(i\), \(1 - x^h/(\theta^h + x^h)\) if \(j\) represses \(i\), and 1 if they don’t interact (\(\theta = \theta_{ij}\), \(h = h_{ij}\)). The phenotype is the steady state that development reaches.

library(grnland)

# edges: "a -> b" activation, "a -| b" repression; self-regulation allowed
m <- grn(c("a -> b", "b -| c", "c -> a", "a -| c"),
         alpha = c(4, 6, 8), theta = 3,
         evolvable = c("alpha", "theta"),   # which parameters are loci
         traits = c("b", "c"))              # which genes are under selection
m
#> <hill_grn> 3 genes, 7 loci, traits: b, c
#> edges: a -> b, a -| c, b -| c, c -> a
#> loci: alpha[a], alpha[b], alpha[c], theta[a,c], theta[b,a], theta[c,a], theta[c,b]

regulation can also be a matrix where regulation[i, j] is the effect of gene j on gene i (+1, -1 or 0). evolvable accepts whole parameter classes ("alpha", "gamma", "theta", "hill") or single entries ("alpha[b]", "theta[c,a]").

The six motifs of the paper are available as paper_motif(1) to paper_motif(6).

Arbitrary dynamics: grn_custom()

For regulatory logic that the Hill model cannot express (additive inputs, basal expression, other kinetics), give the right-hand side of the ODE directly. This runs in R, so it is slower.

m <- grn_custom(
  function(x, p) c(p[["a1"]] - x[1],
                   p[["a2"]] * (0.2 + x[1] / (5 + x[1])) - x[2]),
  params = c(a1 = 2, a2 = 2), genes = c("x1", "x2"))

Genotype-phenotype map 

g <- default_genotype(m)            # or genotype_at(m, phenotype)
phenotype(m, g)                     # steady-state trait values
develop(m, g)                       # all genes plus status (stable / failed)
sensitivity(m, g)                   # J, df/dp and S = dx*/dp = -J^{-1} df/dp
m_matrix(m, g, mu = 0.01, sigma = 0.05, ploidy = 1)   # M = S Sigma S'

Development integrates the ODE (Dormand–Prince 5(4)) from a starting state, polishes the steady state with Newton’s method and checks that it is stable. In networks with several stable states, the starting state (x_start) decides which one is reached; during simulations each offspring starts from its parent’s state.

Landscapes

A landscape is any function from a phenotype matrix (one row per individual) to fitness values. There are constructors for common cases:

landscape_perlin(frequency = 0.5, seed = 1245)            # 2D or 3D Perlin noise
landscape_gaussian(rbind(c(4, 2), c(2, 5)), omega = 1)    # Gaussian peaks, any dimension
landscape_smoothmax(l1, l2, beta = 100)                   # smooth maximum of landscapes
landscape_grid(landscape_perlin(0.5, 1245))               # cached 2D grid (~3x faster sims)
find_peaks(land, lower = 0, upper = 15)                   # local optima

Simulation 

land <- landscape_grid(landscape_perlin(frequency = 0.5, seed = 1245))
peaks <- find_peaks(land, 0, 15)
sim <- simulate_population(
  paper_motif(1), land, start = c(4, 6),
  N = 1000, generations = 10000, mu = 0.01, sigma = 0.05,
  ploidy = 1, reproduction = "clonal",          # or ploidy = 2, "sexual"
  selection = selection_relative_min(),         # or selection_proportional(), selection_exponential(s)
  stop = stop_at_peaks(peaks), record_m = TRUE, seed = 1)
sim$outcome       # index of the peak reached (NA if none)
sim$trajectory    # means, phenotypic (co)variances P_*, M_*, mean fitness per recorded generation

The defaults reproduce the settings of the paper’s scripts: haploid clonal populations of 1000, per-locus mutation rate 0.01, mutational sd 0.05, alleles truncated at 0, the w - min(w) + 0.001 selection weights and the “half the population within ±0.1 of a peak” convergence rule. inst/examples/grid_screen.R shows a full grid screen of starting points.

Differences from the original analysis scripts

  • Steady states are computed numerically for every network, not from closed forms. For the six motifs they agree with the closed forms to about 1e-8, and the sensitivities agree with the analytical expressions in Fig2.r (see tests/testthat/test-motifs.R).
  • Motif 5 (mutual activation): when \(\alpha_1\alpha_2 < \theta^2\) the network goes to the zero state, which is what the dynamics do; the closed form gives negative expression there. The stale-phenotype bug of Fig5.r does not exist here: phenotypes are always recomputed from the mutated genotype.
  • Individuals whose development fails (no stable steady state) get zero fitness by default (invalid = "lethal"); invalid = "reject" discards the offending mutation instead.
  • Random numbers are drawn differently, so runs reproduce the paper’s results statistically, not draw for draw.
